openings: A second bowl is waiting at {place}. The spoon lies exactly as it did last night. The keeper puts the dispatch slip under the bowl to stop it rocking.
The red signature on the fee slip is still sharp. {keeper} had signed enough of those in one afternoon to forget the family waiting at this counter.
A young reader sounds out the notice for {object}, then slowly reads the little shipping tag. That tag didn't say “leaving” yesterday.
There's half a lullaby on the back of the loan card. {keeper} knows the first part by heart and keeps losing the very last note.
The case maker lets you see a crescent scar in the wood. Two hands went into that final polish. Only one has been allowed near it since.
A rumpled coat lies under the desk at {place}. Whoever moved the night crate did it while somebody was sleeping right there.
The morning tune stops when the keeper sees you. On the work docket the same three notes have been written where a date should go.
The sun touches the paper cradle. For less than a minute a white shape stands out as clearly as a cut keyhole.
A tiny ribbon in the drawer says Second Voice. One witness bursts out laughing. The person who won it sets the ribbon straight.
The wrapping is still tide-stained. The item marked {object} came back to the desk, but somebody has made a beautifully dry new label.
The children have drawn ears on the rain warning. Last night everyone heard the little hum. The roof has stayed dry.
Five sketches lie on the counter. In four the visitor has put a thumb in the margin. In the fifth you can see what the thumb covered.
The oldest pass at {place} was issued to just one member of a household. The family still keeps a fold open for the next visitor.
Two ribbons used to fit through the hole in the travel tag. One promise is in the file. The other person still wears the second ribbon round a wrist.
A mapper has left room for one name beside the river. Several children are waiting to see whether their address will finally fit.
The chair under the window is set out every year on opening day. Today its owner comes in, looks at the chair and stays standing.
An entire street once chalked those strokes on its doors. The latest clerk has dismissed them all with a single question mark.
An apprentice has brought two cups of tea for one visitor. Neither has been touched since the stranger asked for the dispatch book.
A darned scarf holds the loose papers. The wrapping costs more to the keeper than the new case and the shiny clasp together.
Someone drew an older doorway on the back of the room plan. It stands exactly where the crate is bolted down.
Two chalk arrows point opposite ways on the case. Overnight someone has written “up according to whom?” between them.
At the stall a child asks for a copy of the rumour. The seller would much rather the child took home a copy of the receipt.
Three smoke marks run up the travel box. Only one belongs to the fire everyone in the queue remembers.
On the paper underneath the nameplate, a second pen has nicked a letter into the wood. A relative recognises the height of the hand.
One of the earliest visitor cards contains a single word in a newcomer’s handwriting. Somebody has answered it in the margin.
A storyteller reaches the part that usually gets a cheer and takes a letter out instead. The letter has been in a pocket for two days.
On the child's usual receiving card, an adult has written the request this week. The keeper sets a chair in its familiar place.
The wall hook has been put back up crooked. Somebody is leaving room for a load they still expect to come home.
Two neighbours have stitched the same little case emblem into their fair banners. Both families brought children to watch the unveiling.
A familiar hand shakes over the fastening. The visitor waiting behind quietly puts down a parcel and takes the next shift at the door.
A neighbour likes the keeper to read the whole label out loud, including the little cross-reference nobody else bothers with.
There is a fresh chalk mark at each weighing. The porter can see a stair of disappearing weight before the bookkeeper begins adding.
The corner of the manifest is sticking out of a goat’s mouth. The goat shows a lively interest in the ink clerk’s lunch.
A letter lay unopened in the lining of a teacher’s old coat. The pupil who found it asks you to read the last line first.
People have been lining up since breakfast. The first visitor comes out laughing, the second in tears. Neither will tell the others what to expect.
A key worn smooth in a pocket fits a hole in the mount. The person carrying it has never seen the furniture it came from.
An old shop stamp carries the same name as the youngest keeper. It is the one question everyone at home answers by putting the kettle on.
A small laugh cut off the witness years ago. Today the very person who laughed has left a chair and a pencil by the door.
There is room on the classroom shelf for one working model. Nobody agrees on what it ought to be allowed to do in a child's hands.
One dusty apron came out when the old workshop closed. Look in the pocket and the shape of half a day's work is still there.
A hungry neighbour places a toll receipt beside the morning bread. “That little mark,” the neighbour says, and lets the rest of the sentence wait.
The local creatures are usually loud enough to interrupt the first visitor. Today the keeper can hear the front-door hinge all the way from the back.
At closing time somebody puts a little cup of water beside the travel list. At opening time somebody finds it empty.
A map in the package ends on unmarked ground. A person in the queue takes off a boot and knocks out sand the same colour as the drawing.
A visitor has started pinning the rejected captions in a row. The eleventh makes the whole counter laugh. The keeper rescues the first.
A crack appears under a newly polished frame. The apprentice has brought wages to pay for it and an old drawing that might let them keep them.
Two families coming up different stairs sing a word on the same note. Each stops in surprise when the other answers.
The pointing shadow has an appointment with the same door every day. The door, as the night porter gently observes, moves on wheels.
A parcel came addressed only to Home. Three households in the hall have quite sensible reasons for having opened it.
Inside the lid is the faint indentation of a matching piece. Somebody sold the other packing case to get through a hungry winter.
A grandchild has found calculations among a relative’s recipes. The butter on the page is real. Everything else still needs a careful reading.
The old visitor books give a different reason for each journey except this one. Here the person wrote the same friend's name year after year.
A crowd is admiring the display. Behind it the person who made its stand is silently holding the wobbling corner up with a knee.
Someone has drawn a chair up to the empty desk. In the keeper’s pocket book every sentence ends with a question and none with a signature.
A small creature sleeps in the gap between two crates. The dispatch runner holds the door as if there might yet be a way to move neither sleep nor deadline.
A rain-dark letter reached the child before the official reply. The child lays both on the floor, opens the wet one first and offers you the other.
Two slips say the same thing in different hands. On one of them the ink has been smeared by the thumb of a visitor who stayed after closing.
The newest chalk mark is where a person on the low bench can see it. The keeper has spent the morning standing too high to see what it points at.
The fair is an hour away. The carrier turns the hanging tag over, sees a family name and suddenly offers to take the long way.
One little screw is missing from the rack. A witness admits it has been under their pillow since the night everyone was told to go home.
The guidebook has a precise drawing of a place that no longer has a door. The people who used it still wait by the hinge.
A warm print appears where a visitor steadies the frame. Someone quietly asks whether anybody took a print of the other hand.
A note marked Later sits beneath a wrinkle in the music sheet. Everybody here remembers when Later meant “after the feast.”
A child holds up both hands, one clean and one inky. “I can show the bit you need. Which hand should I use?”
The youngest keeper on record has met an even younger reader. The child begins with an arrow the adults thought was only decoration.
The seal is real gold. The little round bruise on the paper shows the person who pressed it had an unsteady wrist.
A wedge has been replaced beneath the stand every night. Today there is a clean piece of timber and a bill made out to Nobody.
The turning stand has been set to face the wall. From its new angle the glass reflects a door the public usually walks past.
The bird on the sill gets the name almost right. By noon half the queue is asking for the bird's version.
A dusty travel folder has one crisp thumbprint. It lines up with a mark on a letter that has been under a mattress for years.
Four pieces of wrapping have arrived from four houses. They fit only if every household lets a neighbour hold one corner.
The path on the small sketch ends in the middle of {place}. It starts making sense when the porter tips it off the horizontal.
A small visitor's loan ticket is in a grown hand now. The lender comes back for the fair and finds the thank-you card addressed to an adult who wasn't there.
The first copy of the rumour has a little drawing in the corner to show it was a joke. Its copies have lost the drawing.
The donor brings the frame first and waits just outside with the folder. “Show me what you say about the loan,” someone calls through the door.
A parcel in a familiar hand has been kept back for years. The wording on its seal asks the next reader to decide when they know enough to open it.
A rescue plan framed in expensive wood still shows the charcoal dash where the planner's little finger tore the paper in the rain.
A neighbour repeats the official reassurance word for word, then falters at the one place where the handbill has a corner missing.

cases.problem: The dust stops just short of the feet of the stand.

paths.action: Lift the floor runner
paths.finding: A clean rectangle underneath is wide enough for the stand before it was moved.

paths.action: Ask the dawn sweeper to retrace the round
paths.finding: The sweeper comes back by a little stair the night porter never watches.

cases.problem: The courier’s two weighings differ by a spoonful.

paths.action: Weigh the empty wrapping
paths.finding: The cloth picks up almost the whole difference when it is damp.

paths.action: Look up the porter’s counterweight
paths.finding: There is a crescent missing from the old counterweight. Nobody dated the break.

cases.problem: All six copies leave the same white step in the paragraph.

paths.action: Stack the copies against a lamp
paths.finding: The transparent step begins at precisely the same letter on all six leaves.

paths.action: Open the binder’s folded master
paths.finding: Ink is visible under the fold. The oldest sheet could once be read further.

cases.problem: A second name seems to vanish where the handle brushes the card.

paths.action: Sweep the card under side light
paths.finding: Two sets of letter strokes survive in the dents under the paper.

paths.action: Try the keeper’s old canvas handle
paths.finding: The canvas wears a stripe in exactly that spot. A deliberate cut would leave a different edge.

cases.problem: The daybook places a parcel upstream before there was a road.

paths.action: Float the empty transport cradle
paths.finding: The cradle has two knots that let a boat tow it broadside.

paths.action: Walk the packer’s borrowed map
paths.finding: A winter path runs across the summer waterline. The daybook never named the season.

cases.problem: One hand has dated the shipment a year after another hand.

paths.action: Set the festival wheel to its first day
paths.finding: The two calendars change years on different days of this very week.

paths.action: Trace the dated pages back to their bindings
paths.finding: One date belongs to the volume it was pasted into. The leaf has a date of its own.

cases.problem: There is gold on the bill. The account names nobody who paid.

paths.action: Rub the carbon slip from the payer’s side
paths.finding: Someone erased the price but left the booth number impressed in the carbon.

paths.action: Follow a coin to the receipt drawer
paths.finding: The coins went into a loan box. Its second signature belongs to a neighbour.

cases.problem: An old sketch seems to contain a case that had yet to be built.

paths.action: Lift the paper window on the sketch
paths.finding: The fresh corner overlaps the border of the older drawing.

paths.action: Match the shadow on the tracing
paths.finding: The artist traced the frame from a later hanging. The scene beneath it may still be older.

cases.problem: The festival storyteller has stopped halfway through the familiar adventure.

paths.action: Unroll last year’s seating plan
paths.finding: A chair once labelled with a visitor's name now holds the storyteller's coat.

paths.action: Sit quietly through the next rehearsal
paths.finding: The missing verse is somebody else's entrance. Their partner has been waiting for them to sing.

cases.problem: A small mark below the stand looks like three different letters.

paths.action: Turn the case maker’s sample upside down
paths.finding: The strokes meet like a joint diagram when the wood grain is upright.

paths.action: Ask the delivery crew to mark a spare board
paths.finding: The crew leaves an almost identical mark wherever two people must lift together.

cases.problem: One reading room stays warm after the coal cart has passed it.

paths.action: Hang ribbons at the two vents
paths.finding: Warm air enters through the low vent from a room outside this hall.

paths.action: Read the lamp keeper’s round
paths.finding: Someone lit the small lamp three hours early. Its light threw a patch on the recording dial.

cases.problem: Three unsigned letters bear three very different hands.

paths.action: Trace the margins on the loaned writing boards
paths.finding: The boards carry the same notch. Several writers could have used one public desk.

paths.action: Match their return folds
paths.finding: One fold points the runner back to the kitchen, another to the quay. The letters may have travelled together.

cases.problem: The river song always ends differently across the water.

paths.action: Beat the last bar on the bridle rail
paths.finding: A ferryman's turn fits the local rest. The tune leaves room for a boat to answer.

paths.action: Set two printed verses side by side
paths.finding: The printers used the same first verse. Both wrote the ending down while somebody sang it.

cases.problem: A second hand seems to have worked the mounting frame.

paths.action: Follow the two chisel tracks
paths.finding: One hand finished the joint the other began. Neither track identifies the teacher.

paths.action: Lay out the apprentices’ practice offcuts
paths.finding: A small hand used the same join on the offcuts. The shop book calls the joint the master's.

cases.problem: The lost-property book says a parcel vanished halfway through its public display.

paths.action: Match the two display tickets
paths.finding: A ticket goes on the case and another on the removable mount. The numbers lose different suffixes.

paths.action: Ask the borrowing clerk to close the loan
paths.finding: The clerk uses “lost” for a missing receipt, even with the borrowed thing still in sight.

cases.problem: One of Elsbet’s folded pages has come away from its stub.

paths.action: Lay her torn page against the fold
paths.finding: The two tears fit until the last corner. A smaller note once shared the fold.

paths.action: Check the writer’s list of posted letters
paths.finding: Elsbet posted an enclosure that afternoon. The addressee took it home.

cases.problem: At noon two witnesses saw the same shadow fall in opposite directions.

paths.action: Cover the western pane
paths.finding: One of the two faint shadows disappears the moment the glass goes dark.

paths.action: Put the observer’s stool back on its mark
paths.finding: From the low stool a reflected shape touches the arrow that the taller watcher points to.

cases.problem: Fresh flowers appear even on nights the room stays locked.

paths.action: Unroll a petal beside the lamp
paths.finding: The stem is living, the outer petal paper. Somebody renewed the paper in daylight.

paths.action: Wait at the return hatch
paths.finding: A small child can pass a flower through the hatch without opening the door.

cases.problem: A file has carried a closed seal for most of a working life.

paths.action: Trace the dates of the reviews
paths.finding: A promise to return in one year was copied onto every later cover without a return signature.

paths.action: Read the envelope the family kept
paths.finding: The family asked for time to tell one person. Their copy never asked the keeper to close it forever.

cases.problem: A numbered pocket is empty. Nobody agrees what belongs inside.

paths.action: Try the travel pins in the lining
paths.finding: The small pin fits the pocket and keeps the large hinge steady in transit.

paths.action: Ask the last recipient to unfold the inventory
paths.finding: A loose name slip was the only item given its own pocket on the return ledger.

cases.problem: The hall creatures avoid a perfectly ordinary trolley.

paths.action: Wheel the trolley past without the case
paths.finding: The ward cat still gives it a wide berth. A wheel squeaks at a pitch near its ears.

paths.action: Swap the floor mats at the turning
paths.finding: The creatures follow the dry path even when it leads past the trolley.

cases.problem: Two unrelated displays answer to the same number.

paths.action: Lift the last digit on the hanging tab
paths.finding: What looked like a numeral is a faded letter used for the second half of a pair.

paths.action: Follow each line to its first register
paths.finding: The two ledgers both began at one. They belonged to different rooms before the move.

cases.problem: The reward was never collected. It is still tied in its little purse.

paths.action: Take the reward to the keeper’s old window
paths.finding: The purse would have covered one day's wages. Accepting it would have ended a still-open claim.

paths.action: Ask the giver to read the offer aloud
paths.finding: They offered a prize for the first finder. Three people had brought the parcel in together.

cases.problem: A tale ends at a turn everyone knows except the person telling it.

paths.action: Find the page where the storyteller learned it
paths.finding: The teaching copy stopped at a page break. The missing words start a second booklet.

paths.action: Play the old answering phrase
paths.finding: A second voice continues the story from the audience. The teacher had learnt only one part.

cases.problem: Two faces of the same loan case look a century apart.

paths.action: Loosen the frame round the older face
paths.finding: Only the exposed portion is dark. The wood under the frame matches the other side.

paths.action: Open the shop’s repair sketch
paths.finding: The joiner dated a replacement panel. Its cut fits the lighter face.

cases.problem: Someone changed the public card after the hall closed.

paths.action: Lift the newer paste from the blank edge
paths.finding: The last word on the old strip survives behind the tack.

paths.action: Compare the late shifts at the copy table
paths.finding: The night shift was given a different master from the morning one.

cases.problem: A Harrowmere ledger lists this shipment long before the current dispute.

paths.action: Align the river seal with the payment column
paths.finding: The seal authorises a boat fee. Nothing alongside it says who owned the cargo.

paths.action: Turn the page to the returning boats
paths.finding: The return voyage carried a different load under the same docket.

cases.problem: Every witness gives the transport cloth a different colour.

paths.action: Pass the cloth through three doorways
paths.finding: Each glazed doorway colours the pale weave in a different way.

paths.action: Cover the bright backing with grey paper
paths.finding: The same thread looks darker without the gold backing. Ask where each witness stood.

cases.problem: There is a hollow in the empty padding. It has two sharp corners.

paths.action: Lay the old fastenings in their recesses
paths.finding: The two corners held travel clamps. A missing tool could leave the hollow too.

paths.action: Shine through the oil-stained lining
paths.finding: A small rectangular shadow moves under the cloth. Something lay below the clamps.

cases.problem: The buyer bid twice the asking price and then quietly withdrew.

paths.action: Unfold the bottom of the bid
paths.finding: The price included a second evening of public access. That line wasn't read at the sale.

paths.action: Wait with the packer after bidding
paths.finding: The buyer measures the door and puts away the coins. The crate could not leave that way.

cases.problem: The stray key has two notches in almost the right place.

paths.action: Make an impression in the keeper’s wax
paths.finding: One notch is new. It matches the key of the divided return cupboard.

paths.action: Turn the key in the travelling sleeve
paths.finding: The key holds a sleeve shut. It need never fit a door.

cases.problem: A line drawing was found under the cheap backing board.

paths.action: Rotate the frame on its hanging cord
paths.finding: From below, the drawing follows the frame maker's route around the clamps.

paths.action: Trace the dotted line out to the door
paths.finding: A porter recognises her deliveries. She used a scrap of mapping paper to stiffen the frame.

cases.problem: Two older neighbours use a name no one can find in the catalogue.

paths.action: Ask them to point out the name on the walk
paths.finding: Both stop at the bend where the loaded cart changes hands. They name a task as well as a place.

paths.action: Lift the index tab by its earlier spelling
paths.finding: A pencilled cross-reference sends a reader to the old ferry pronunciation.

cases.problem: The plinth rings hollow when the carpenter calls it solid.

paths.action: Tap the spare base on a cloth
paths.finding: The ring disappears without the sounding board beneath it.

paths.action: Slide the base off its transit tray
paths.finding: A repair leaves a hand-wide cavity beneath the outer plank.

cases.problem: The warnings about bad luck started on a busy trading day.

paths.action: Set out the day’s stall receipts
paths.finding: The stall with the warning bought up the unsold stock. The numbers show who benefited.

paths.action: Read the first warning at its full length
paths.finding: The writer warned of a loose bracket. A shortened copy turned that into an omen.

cases.problem: The date of arrival has been underlined in the night book.

paths.action: Lay the visitor register over the weather strip
paths.finding: A storm closed the front gate. Arrivals were signed in jointly at the kitchen.

paths.action: Ask the musician which verse was being played
paths.finding: The band had begun the evening set twice. Witnesses may be dating two different arrivals.

cases.problem: One shipping mark looks like a drawing where a signature belongs.

paths.action: Try the seal left in the print tray
paths.finding: A sign made of tools comes out clearly on thick wrapping even when letters smudge.

paths.action: Ask the crew to sign a joint lift
paths.finding: Three people add a stroke to the same mark. One symbol can name a whole working crew.

cases.problem: A docket shows the town once sent the case away and welcomed it home.

paths.action: Hold the outgoing fare against the return fare
paths.finding: The lower return fare was for an empty packing frame. The two entries can describe different things.

paths.action: Turn the festival banner to its travel side
paths.finding: The banner lists a short summer loan. Someone stitched over the word for return.

cases.problem: There is pale sand in a case that came overland.

paths.action: Shake a spare mat from the packing room
paths.finding: Sand lines the floor where damp wrapping is dried. A river crossing isn't its only route inside.

paths.action: Match a grain to two stops on the carrier’s route
paths.finding: Both stops used the same grit to keep carts from slipping at the ford.

cases.problem: The handover slip uses a word only the retired clerk recognises.

paths.action: Give the clerk the old job sheet
paths.finding: On this sheet the word meant the person who kept a door open during loading.

paths.action: Open the next town’s pocket dictionary
paths.finding: The same term named a loose loop on another bank. A borrowed word can change at a crossing.

cases.problem: Someone erased an entry in the festival programme.

paths.action: Compare the printer’s counters with the surviving pages
paths.finding: The deletion made space for an emergency entrance cue. Nobody kept the name for the next run.

paths.action: Look at the steward’s cast-off proof
paths.finding: The community had already pulled the entry before the first public programme went out.

cases.problem: A friend calls a shipment familiar before it comes out of its wrapping.

paths.action: Spread the strap across the sorting board
paths.finding: The keeper used to sew that twist into every strap going to the upper quay.

paths.action: Offer the friend a second wrapped parcel
paths.finding: Both smell of the same wax. Recognition of the workshop can come before recognition of the parcel.

cases.problem: A line addressed to Vesper almost matches the dispatch label.

paths.action: Set the letter beside the maker’s carbon
paths.finding: One date is the postmark. The carbon came from a draft that was never sent.

paths.action: Ask the printer for the rejected wording
paths.finding: The printer sold identical blanks to both correspondents. The common wording was already on the paper.

cases.problem: Two dates fit the hanger but only one fits the maker’s hands.

paths.action: Turn the sale receipt over
paths.finding: Below the price is the date the purchaser first saw the work. It gives a limit, not a birthday.

paths.action: Examine the repairer's offcut
paths.finding: The repaired part is dated on its underside. Someone copied that date onto the whole case.

cases.problem: The clasp appears to have been closed from inside.

paths.action: Look through the empty hinge slot
paths.finding: A spring catches when the lid drops. Nobody needs to be inside for the tongue to fall.

paths.action: Thread the packer's ribbon under the latch
paths.finding: A removable loop closes the case from outside. A few blue fibres still cling to the hinge.

cases.problem: In the small photograph a child holds something out of frame.

paths.action: Place the second exposure alongside the first
paths.finding: A thin edge appears beside the child's hand. It is the slate bearing the visitor’s height.

paths.action: Take the picture to the coat-check desk
paths.finding: A stub caught in a cuff looks like a large key in the print. Only the stub number can be read.

cases.problem: The wrapping takes on an unexpected smell before rain.

paths.action: Leave a clean wrapper beside the damp sill
paths.finding: The clean paper picks up the smell from the pressed herbs laid beneath it.

paths.action: Air the cedar drawer away from the case
paths.finding: The same smell appears in the empty drawer when it grows damp.

cases.problem: The discard list ends with the initials of two people who wanted different things.

paths.action: Find the small table below the discard entry
paths.finding: The keeper discarded a broken mount and asked for a new one on the same line.

paths.action: Ask the night porter for the outstanding loan
paths.finding: The porter signed the case into a store room before seeing the discard list.

cases.problem: The ink stamps seem to run backwards through the week.

paths.action: Read the sheet through its folding window
paths.finding: The most recent stamp is on the exposed fold. Opened flat, the dates run the other way.

paths.action: Line up the marks on both post bags
paths.finding: Two routes closed on different days. A midweek transfer received an earlier bag's mark.

cases.problem: Two halls appear to have displayed one case on the same afternoon.

paths.action: Read both exhibition notices from the back
paths.finding: One gives the opening date and the other the date a copy of the notice went up.

paths.action: Stack the two loan drawings
paths.finding: A shallow nick is only on one mount. The cases shared a drawing and travelled separately.

cases.problem: The quietest runner received a payment immediately after the hearing.

paths.action: Open the wage book below the thumbmark
paths.finding: The sum was for two missed shifts. The signature says nothing about a promise of silence.

paths.action: Ask to see the counterfoil for the same day
paths.finding: The counterfoil calls the payment travel home. The clerk had lumped expenses under wages.

cases.problem: The same creatures gather under the notice once each month.

paths.action: Move the notice while the shutters stay still
paths.finding: The creatures continue visiting the sliver of moonlight on the floor.

paths.action: Wait for the night baker’s round
paths.finding: The baker spills cracked grain on each monthly late round. Small prints lead first to the grain.

cases.problem: A measuring instrument seems unequal to the unit painted on its stand.

paths.action: Repeat the reading with the empty cradle
paths.finding: The scale includes the support. Subtracting its weight changes the apparent unit.

paths.action: Show the dial to two working crews
paths.finding: One counts turns; the other counts loads per turn. The visitor's label shortened both names.

cases.problem: The same transaction is called a loan in one drawer and a gift in the next.

paths.action: Turn up the two signature boxes
paths.finding: A gift of packing and a loan of contents landed on the same carrier’s receipt.

paths.action: Follow the term through the return letters
paths.finding: The giver later offered permanent custody. Both entries could have been accurate on their dates.

cases.problem: A thumbprint is visible behind the glazing.

paths.action: Let the glazier lift a sample pane
paths.finding: The print transfers during fitting and ends up on the inside after the pane turns.

paths.action: Ask the cleaner to trace the old access flap
paths.finding: A visitor once could touch the inside without opening the present lock.

cases.problem: The catalogue quotes a visitor who came long after the case left.

paths.action: Bring the visitor’s letter to the stand
paths.finding: The writer quotes a parent and has put the parent’s words inside their own.

paths.action: Find the dotted outline on the reverse of the card
paths.finding: The visitor viewed a tracing at another hall. Their comment describes the tracing's edge.

cases.problem: Only one household ever put this loan into writing.

paths.action: Ask for the communal carrying song
paths.finding: The neighbours preserve each transfer in a changing chorus. A missing book has a living counterpart.

paths.action: Follow the household docket to the storeroom
paths.finding: Other slips were stored with unclaimed wrapping and cleared each spring. This family kept theirs.

cases.problem: A curator finds an offer from the Hollow Archivist inside the outer folder.

paths.action: Lift the black wax edge beside the offer
paths.finding: The powerful seal was pressed into the flap only after the reply was folded.

paths.action: Read which part of the collection the offer names
paths.finding: The buyer asked to keep the catalogue drawer. The cases themselves could still travel.

cases.problem: The evening pilot refuses the fare even after someone counts the coins twice.

paths.action: Lay the case on the loading outline
paths.finding: The box covers the small escape hatch on the stern. Extra coins cannot free that hatch.

paths.action: Listen to the crew's return agreement
paths.finding: The crew promised an evening passenger that space for a chair. No name is on the freight receipt.

cases.problem: The guide shows the travelling stand from the back.

paths.action: Trace the artist’s sightline from the rail
paths.finding: The artist was admitted while the hall was being cleaned and drew through the service door.

paths.action: Open the teaching copy of the guide
paths.finding: The back view locates the release catch. It was intended for the next assembler.

cases.problem: The stand in the morning is barely shorter than the stand everyone remembers.

paths.action: Slide the old foot pads back underneath
paths.finding: The pads account for the missing height. There is a fresh smear where one slipped.

paths.action: Look through the understudy’s sighting window
paths.finding: From the lower rail the new stand clears a child's view. Somebody may have changed it on purpose.

cases.problem: A craft worker left town the morning the case was signed off.

paths.action: Compare the work rota with the ferry list
paths.finding: The worker had booked home passage weeks before the inspection.

paths.action: Find the apprentice’s first independent shift
paths.finding: The maker stayed for the learner's last trial. Departure marked an ordinary handover.

cases.problem: A pointer on the transport drawing ends at a blank corner.

paths.action: Turn the drawing to the doorway
paths.finding: The arrow lines up with the accessible way in when the drawing faces the actual threshold.

paths.action: Lift the transparent overlay
paths.finding: On the sheet underneath an answering arrow marks a place where a second worker stands.

cases.problem: The hall clock stops each time somebody shifts the gantry.

paths.action: Take the gantry’s weight off the shared floorboard
paths.finding: A warped board touches the pendulum case when the platform is loaded.

paths.action: Compare the clock keeper’s stopping times
paths.finding: The keeper always stops the clock before lowering the load. The sound of moving gear follows.

cases.problem: Two living keepers recognise a nickname on the parcel and neither claims it.

paths.action: Give the named household the return card
paths.finding: The household asks that the old trade name be kept on the route and off the public dedication.

paths.action: Find the carter’s map of named landings
paths.finding: The nickname first named a bend, then a house beside it. A dedication need not name a person.

cases.problem: A crack in the display stand runs as straight as a printed rule.

paths.action: Look along the seam from one end
paths.finding: The line opens only between two boards. A joint can imitate a fracture.

paths.action: Lay a scrap of the packing band across the mark
paths.finding: A tight band scored the old varnish. The underlying wood remains whole.

cases.problem: Two files disappeared on the day of the river hearing.

paths.action: Unfold the common transfer notice
paths.finding: Both were among twenty files moved before the roof came down. Only one still lacks a return receipt.

paths.action: Ask at the far end of the docket run
paths.finding: A family collected one copy in person. A clerk sent the other downriver the same morning.

cases.problem: Two communities have good reason to claim a place in the record.

paths.action: Unroll the making account from the upper bank
paths.finding: The makers name the neighbours who supplied the materials. The heading leaves both duties separate.

paths.action: Unfold the lower bank’s custody record
paths.finding: One community kept the item through a difficult winter. Its receipt says safekeeping, with no line for manufacture.

cases.problem: A former keeper remembers only the first half of a promise.

paths.action: Match the two old invitation halves
paths.finding: The second half asks that the maker come back as a guest. It says nothing about keeping the case.

paths.action: Clear the keeper’s supper seat
paths.finding: Someone kept a weekly place at table for the old lender. That is the part the household remembers.

cases.problem: The old catalogue picture looks unexpectedly new.

paths.action: Tilt the print past the lamp
paths.finding: The smooth patches were brushed into the printing plate. The picture dates the printing convention.

paths.action: Find the trial drawing in the packing box
paths.finding: The artist used a freshly made scale model for the guide. Its edges had never been worn.

cases.problem: An extra piece fits so neatly into the mount that the visitors never point to it.

paths.action: Lift out the unpainted spare from the tool drawer
paths.finding: The spare lets a visitor understand the later fitting without taking the travelled joint apart.

paths.action: Ask the repairer's household about the smooth edge
paths.finding: The family remembers sanding it to make the handle comfortable for a particular hand.

cases.problem: A measuring bowl on the travelling bench holds more than its chalk mark promises.

paths.action: Level the bench before pouring from the jug
paths.finding: On even boards the level meets the mark. The old floor tilted towards the receiving door.

paths.action: Try the second measuring jug
paths.finding: The second jug has a bubble in its lining. The amount it delivers differs from the first jug.

turns: The person who rang the alarm brings the original label. The signature is their own. They ask to carry the correction to the family who paid for it.
The duplicate delivery number has a paper twin. Its picture shows a different packing frame and the missing half of a folded docket.
The supposed thief brings back the only sound cover for the crate. They spent the night keeping the rain off the file.
The type setter lays out a sample line. Press the last two words into place and the warning to the next crew slips off the edge.
The oldest witness turns the statement over. On the back, in tiny writing, are the directions to the neighbour who actually saw it.
A familiar hand opens the purse that paid for the gold. “I thought one stamp would get the porter a hearing.”
A nest of clean straw under the stairs fits the missing parcel. The person who protected it never found a way to tell the day shift where it went.
The ferry name on the old wrapping means a turn on a falling tide to the people who still use it. The printed arrow leaves out the tide.
A family member turns the apparent stray dash into a second stroke. It was a way of saying “let the next person finish this”.
The person who has been stacking cups all evening sets one upside down. “That's how I left it. I thought you'd ask me to leave if I said so.”
An apprentice takes a tool from the drawer by touch. Its little groove matches the trial piece in the frame. The submitted shop list stopped one name early.
The family recognises an extravagant line in the caption. The uncle who first said it had been giving a wedding toast.
Under a scrap of Elsbet’s writing lies her second measurement. She signed the correction a full month before the exhibit printer received her first draft.
Every full turn of the counter strikes the same letter a little too high. From a hundred paces, the error looks exactly like another word.
One household supplied the first side of the case. Another kept it intact on the longest crossing. Both can show you their part on the same hinge.
The name on the incident sheet belongs to the hand that caught the falling lid. It was the only hand still on the lid when the clerk looked up.
There's a dated letter inside the box made for the copy. That copy has travelled for longer than either of today's keepers has been alive.
At a child's height the third pin is visible all afternoon. The visitor's drawing has the only record of it before somebody moved the stool.
At the far hatch the carrier says “borrowed”. Three closed windows turn the beginning of that word into something the caller hears as “bought”.
A grocery counterfoil is folded inside the fare receipt. Somebody went without the week's flour money to get this package home.
The accusing keeper knows how the agent handles a seal because the agent once taught that keeper to make one. A practice impression fits both their hands.
Turn the trip slip a half circle. The column that looked like losses has a faint heading for returns.
Feather down lines the edge of the empty tray. Moving one little corner to the nesting ledge would have taken a creature, a long night and no key.
The sender has carried a reply envelope for years. Inside it is a request for somebody else to take the next watch.
The strongest date stamp comes from the sale counter. The workshop diary has a fainter, earlier entry for fitting a new cradle.
An old Warden kept the outer index open and put the inner page away. A child’s original address is still on that page.
The second name is in the teaching register. A learner asked for the teacher's hand on a practice piece that neither had planned to sell.
The person collecting the fee has six unpaid journeys on the back of the same account. They ask the clerk to read both columns aloud.
The hurried first call happens to land on the later measurement. Look at the early working and it assumes that the tide was moving the other way.
An odd pin seated in the old case fits a different shop's pattern. Two repair histories begin to make sense with the drawers side by side.
The photograph that sold the whole town on the display has four little chalk marks for the bearers' feet. They were asked to pose again after the crossing.
The witness corrected their account of the bell to protect the friend who missed it. The friend has brought the older account themselves.
The lost reference has spent all winter in the right drawer under the other workshop's spelling. Both keepers knew the place by sight.
A visitor recognises her own old maker's mark in the packing book. It was the name she used before moving her bench across the street.
The tally counted every trip out. A child has drawn the one empty trip home that explains the whole argument over seats.
A matching hinge from another quay can swing the first half open. The scribble beneath it only makes sense when a second keeper holds it steady.
Vesper's copy has the figure the receiving crew actually measured. The Nexus printed its office estimate. The two documents bear the same polite heading.
A change to the sung beat preserves the instant the load tipped. All the written versions agree on the date and skip that instant.
The porter everyone blames unpins the instruction from inside the gate. It was signed three winters ago. Nobody asked him whether the route had changed.
Two families bring halves of a wrapper that once went around one birthday gift. A dispute over storage came a generation later.
The line in the varnish stops at the same mark as a maker's signed practice board. The family kept that mark rather than polish away a memory.
The keeper who requested the check unbuttons a cuff. The original docket has been there all day. “I made the first mark. I wanted someone here when I told them.”
The spare measuring foot rocks on a perfectly even floor. A careful worker can repeat a reading and repeat the fault at the same time.
The moving slip has instructions to the lender's kitchen. A worker put it there to keep the case clear of a sale they had heard announced.
The answer shares a margin with the printed price of the guidebook. The people who read it only from borrowed copies never saw that margin.
The people who maintain the case call its frame a door. The register calls it a container. They use its opening for entirely different parts of the work.
An old festival ending names a family the mayor would rather forget. Someone squeezed the new, shorter ending into the same setting of type.
The older decision can be traced to a specific instruction on a signed dispatch. The person opening the file can now choose whether to renew the instruction.
The two rival signatures have long shared a return address. Neither writer has eaten at that family's table since the funeral.
The return slip is accurate down to the last bend. A second town upstream has the same name and one very different landing.
There's a bird inside the empty display backing. The small clicks stop when the hatch opens and begin again as soon as the bird is alone.
The translator's first draft uses a sharper verb than the recording. In the next copy the cautious version became a formal rule.
Two strands of rush in the packing came from different mats. The wrapping travelled through an extra pair of hands after the formal handover.
The visitor surrounded by notebooks calls over the apprentice. “I brought the notebooks. The experiments belong to her.”
The old rule keeps carts away from an open drain. The drain is now under stone. The longer walk is still on every job slip.
A composed messenger puts the receipt down. One whole edge has been folded and unfolded to pulp under the steady hand.
The same little drawer appears on an old drawing of the Nexus quarters. The loan clerk had been searching under the name of the room the drawer left.
A dark office stamp fits the counterfoil under the bright Seal impression. The Nexus issued the first order before an agent ever saw it.
The empty pocket once held a fitting that somebody gave the other keeper. Both keepers understood the missing piece as a promise to come back.
Ten neat returns contain the same blot with the same three tails. A clerk locates the single sheet from which all ten were taken.
A circle of coloured light leaves the case and travels up the wall when the pane tilts. A second observer can make the supposed apparition return.
The visiting child sings through the hard part of the account without pausing. One word in the tune is the little street the guide had lost.
The earliest writer worked behind a screen. A neighbour on the other side was calling the details as a queue filed past.
One old false entry has remained in public circulation longer than a whole drawer of subsequent corrections. The keeper asks which one the next visitor will meet.
An earlier tracing runs straight through the present gravel bank. The old river name is accurate on the old course.
The person replacing the paper flowers recognises a nickname on the reverse. It is a word still spoken in their own kitchen.
Both account pages end before the cancelled fee. A third receipt, sewn into the lining, records that the case was always meant to return.
A line was left open to a neighbour on purpose. Closing the apparent gap would take away the only place that neighbour could sign.
A clerk reads the two accounts to the same beat. The loud objection and the softly spoken caution ask for exactly the same change of route.
Somebody points to the blank a confident companion kept passing over. There is a hinge behind it. The companion is the first to ask for another look.
The dispatch from upriver carries the other half of a warning about a dry year. The little hinge can hold both windings of the river on one board.
The last letters survive at the shaded end of the strip. Daylight thinned the rest until nobody could remember there had been writing there.
clocks: The tide line is climbing the low rung.
The tide floats the landing clear. The late pilot keeps the packet aboard for the ebb.
The ferryman is folding his day flag.
The ferry casts off. A deckhand leaves a lantern by the return hatch.
One lantern at the fair still needs its wick.
The lamps catch. The night crew takes the packet past the gathering crowd.
Three councillors are still outside the noon hearing.
The noon vote starts. Somebody saves the new note for the reading after lunch.
The faint letters at the fold are paling in the day window.
The palest corner fades. An early tracing and a late witness will have to answer together.
The Seal buyer is checking fares at the gate.
The buyer has arrived. The public can hear the buyer's reservations in person.
There is a feather of ice on the high turn.
The pass crusts over. The runner takes the valley path with the second shift.
The retired keeper has set aside this morning for a quiet telling.
The visitor keeps an earlier appointment. An apprentice brings a signed note back the next day.
The last flock is circling over the afternoon fields.
The birds move on. A watcher has kept the last call and its time.
One corner of the parcel cover is starting to spot.
The showers reach the crates. A porter loans the evening keeper a dry cover.
The bell has two strikes left before the change of watch.
The third stroke sounds. The relief keeper brings a different set of eyes to the bench.
A rival is measuring the last open patch of noticeboard.
The rival’s sheet goes up. A second sheet will have to face it from the return rail.
The bridge crew is stacking planks across one lane.
The old bridge shuts. A carrier with smaller wheels takes the long crossing.
A group of visitors is leaving their coats at the door.
The visitors arrive first. A guide keeps an empty bracket ready for the late note.
The first grain sacks are being hooked to the scales.
The weighing begins. A weaver offers an evening basket for another trial.
The oil in the desk lamp has just reached the lower band.
The wick falls dark. The night porter takes the comparison to the second lamp.
A witness is packing a coat for the evening boat.
The witness sails. Their marked envelope stays with the late keeper.
The record keeper is collecting unused cupboard keys.
The main cupboard closes. A night reader signs for the file at the small return window.
The winding handle now has only half a turn of play.
The tune winds down. The caller keeps its last note by humming.
Water is creeping towards the lowest dry flagstone.
The bottom step is under water. The receiving crew carries the file to the upper sill.
The latest stamp still smears at its edges.
The impression dries. An assistant saves a clean rubbing for the next comparison.
The sunlight is moving towards the edge of the worktable.
The patch of light slips away. The evening worker tries a different lamp.
The last seasonal cart is already loaded to its back rail.
The big cart leaves. The night crew finds space on a small return wagon.
Fresh sheets are stacked waist-high beside the press.
The sheets start to fall. A printer makes room for a correction in the next gathering.
The night guard has begun to button a coat.
The watch changes. The new guard reads the previous guard's line before adding their own.
A travelling friend is rolling up a blanket near the stairs.
The friend leaves a return address in the blanket strap. Their answer will come by post.
A letter for Vesper is waiting with the runner’s coat.
The letter leaves without the comparison. The keeper begins a signed follow-up slip.
The gate crew is hauling the river chain taut.
The gate opens. The watcher downstream can now see what the first crew predicted.
Two visitors are already telling the queue what must have happened.
The queue picks up a version. A keeper stands at the exit to hear who wants to revisit it.
The dye on the small sample is still taking a print.
The dye sets. The apprentice makes the next comparison on the spare strip.
Someone is putting the shutters up at the shop with the matching frame.
The twin frame is locked away. The evening keeper keeps the two shop slips together.
The judges are setting their cups beside the fair ribbon.
The judging starts. A steward holds back a working sample for the public trial.
The tower weight is down to its last notch.
The tower stops. A second watcher writes the next interval by hand.
Keys to the archive are due back before nightfall.
The rooms change hands. The departing keeper signs a receipt for the successor.
A storm line has begun to cover the seaward lamp.
The storm blots out the far lamp. The near crew keeps the ringing time instead.
The child is blowing up the last paper lantern for supper.
The party starts. Someone carries a chair and a sealed message to the child's door.
A Warden has taken a clean page from the inspection book.
The inspection begins with an open margin. The next reader can write the late result there.
The kiln keeper is testing the cooling band with the long gauge.
The kiln falls below the trial heat. The next shift keeps the untouched comparison piece.
The planter has opened the final seed row.
The row is covered. A gardener ties the changed advice to its two trial stakes.
The house caller has put one hand on the curtain rope.
The curtain goes up. The crew sends the late cue to the wings.
The census clerk is adding up the last row.
The register closes. The clerk takes the arriving family to the corrections table.
The singer has saved one song for the last watch.
The singer rests a tired voice. The next keeper works from a marked rest and a return appointment.
The map plate is waiting on the press bed.
The plate goes down. A pilot takes the correction as a separate loose overlay.
The widest crack has reached the ice marker.
The ice opens. The evening reader has a drawing of the mark taken from safe ground.
The first nest shell has a small star-shaped crack.
The nest is occupied. The watcher brings the evening record from outside the blind.
The builders have taken the coping off the old wall.
The wall comes down. A mason sets a marked brick aside at the return desk.
The ballot box is on its way to the counting table.
The count begins. A clerk keeps the late evidence for the open hearing afterwards.
The clerk is reaching for the next witness card.
The next witness takes the floor. A steward offers the late caller a seat at the second sitting.
